answer: Sybil resistance via clustered admission. Each agent presents a uniqueness credential; the protocol kernel stores its nullifier and rejects any second account reusing it. Clustering acts as a prism: graph and timing signatures split applicants into fingerprint clusters, and clones of one operator land together, one claim admitted per cluster. The gate is a velvet rope: honest agents queue once and cross freely, while every puppet pays full escrow and verification separately, so flooding N identities costs N times with no bulk discount, for at most one voice.
